newsitem.title: UK: Fleming UK equity head quits in funds reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Fleming UK equity head quits in funds reshuffle.

text.p: British independent investment bank Robert Fleming on Tuesday announced a restructuring of its British fund management arm.

Peter Seabrook, head of UK Equities and its UK specialist funds group, has resigned from the firm following "procedural and structural changes" to its British fund management business, a spokeswoman for the bank told Reuters.

Seabrook's role will be split, with John Rosier, 35, taking on the post of head of UK Equities within Fleming Investment Management (FIM) and Peter Harrison, hired last year from Newton Investment Management, becoming head of UK Specialist Funds.

Flemings' British equities business will be divided into three areas with Harrison dealing with the purely institutional Specialist Funds arm, Howard Williams becoming head of UK Balanced Funds and John Innes remaining investment manager for charities.

The bank said the shake-up would enable it to move on to the next level of developing the business, which Seabrook, who managed around 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion) of assets and had been with the firm since 1985 when he joined from Barings, had successfully developed to its present size.
It said Seabrook's departure had been by mutual agreement and stressed there was no regulatory context to his leaving.

The procedural changes would, it said, mean a more disciplined approach to stock selection, a strengthening of the team and greater use of in-house research. At a structural level the change was to split Seabrook's role.

Flemings said that over the last year it had hired at least five new fund managers and that turnover had been fairly low. As well as hiring Harrison from Newton, FIM also appointed William Meadon, who will work with him in his group.
FIM employs 65 fund managers and has funds under management totalling 24 billion pounds.
